f1.quote: ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermets were consolidated by spark plasma sintering at 1300, 1400, 1500, or 1600 °C to determine the sintering temperature giving the best mechanical properties and resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion and wear.

f2.quote: Corrosion specimens were immersed in molten Al at 700 °C for 4, 8, or 12 days.

f3.quote: Ball-on-disc wear tests used a Si3N4 ball at room temperature, 10 N load, 500 r/min, and 30 min.

f4.quote: At 1500 °C, the liquid high-entropy-alloy binder uniformly filled pores and strongly connected ZrB2 grains, producing the highest relative density (97.71%) and a compact microstructure.

f5.quote: At 1600 °C, binder overflow/loss generated additional pores and reduced relative density to 94.73%.

f6.quote: Relative to cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C, the 1500 °C material should exhibit the greatest density

f8.quote: Relative to cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C, the 1500 °C material should exhibit the greatest ... fracture toughness ... its fracture toughness should also exceed that of pure ZrB2.

f9.quote: Relative to cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C, the 1500 °C material should exhibit ... the lowest molten-Al corrosion rate

f11.quote: Relative to cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C, the 1500 °C material should exhibit ... the lowest ... wear volume
